title: Founder shuts down a 16-agent Claude Code crew and replaces it with one on-call assistant
summary: A founder built 16 scheduled Claude Code agents to run parts of his company, then found he had stopped using them. He replaced them with one assistant that sees per-project context, calendar and email and answers over iMessage.
agent_role: The original agents ran on schedules, handed tasks to each other and sent morning briefings. The replacement assistant answers only when asked, drawing on per-client project folders, calendar, messages and email.
outcome: Author reports sending the agents 56 messages on day one and one or none a week later, so he switched off 26 of 28 scheduled runs and moved to a single assistant.
what_they_did: The poster set up 16 Claude Code agents, each with a company role and schedule, passing tasks between themselves and sending a morning briefing. After usage collapsed, he replaced them with one assistant, 'Optimus', on top of per-client folders with their own context and logs. He texts or sends voice notes via iMessage; his Mac transcribes them locally and Optimus replies in text and voice.
how_it_went: He says the crew generated constant approval requests and a ~100-item task list where he couldn't tell what was done. He found working per project with one assistant that only speaks when asked works much better.
worth_knowing: The assistant runs on his MacBook, so it sleeps when the lid closes; he plans a Mac mini for always-on reachability, not autonomy. He argues autonomy without knowing what matters just adds noise.
prompt: Help me set up a single on-demand assistant for my work. Create one folder per project in [workspace path], each with a context file and a running log. Then read my calendar, email and messages for [accounts] and keep one consolidated list of open tasks and things I'm waiting on. Only respond when I ask; do not run scheduled jobs or contact anyone on your own. When I ask about a project, load only that project's folder. Before sending any email or message or changing my calendar, show me the draft and wait for my approval.

curation.rationale: A first-hand account of running a 16-agent Claude Code crew, with concrete usage numbers and a clear switch to a single on-demand assistant. Useful lessons, but light on setup details and tooling.
